summary: State Representative John R. Plewa submitted a formal letter opposing the proposed Airport Spur, raising objections about cost, lack of travel-time data, insufficient traffic justification for a four-lane facility, noise impacts near an elementary school, and the adequacy of the environmental statement. He proposed an alternative routing via College Avenue with electronic traffic control devices as a less expensive and less disruptive option, and demanded a feasibility study and cost comparison before the final EIS was approved.
complaint_summary: Representative Plewa objects to the proposed Airport Spur on grounds of excessive cost ($12.1 million for 1.5 miles), lack of travel-time savings data, insufficient traffic volume to justify a four-lane facility, noise impacts near Hamlin-Garland Elementary School, and inadequate consideration of a cheaper College Avenue alternative with electronic traffic control.

statement.text:
This letter is for the express purpose of commenting on the 'Draft' Environmental Statement of the Mitchell Field Airport Spur. I will limit my remarks to comments and questions concerning an alternative to the proposed project that seemingly has been overlooked by your staff. I refer to the alternative of routing airport traffic down to the College Avenue interchange down to Howell Avenue and north to General Mitchell Field. I propose that the Department explore the feasibility of this plan:
1. The upgrading of East College Avenue between 15th Street and Howell Avenue, an improvement that is inevitable in the near future.
2. The installation of electronic sensing and traffic control devices which will route airport traffic to College Avenue when the Layton Avenue route becomes overcrowded.
My plan offers these advantages:
1. It will be far less expensive than the proposed $12.1 million project that is presently scheduled for construction. There will be no cost for construction of an interchange; maintenance costs in the future will be lower with the responsibility for one road instead of two.
2. It expropriates less land than the proposed spur, a resource that is growing scarcer every year in the Milwaukee area with increased demands for residential and commercial development.
3. It protects the little children in the Hamlin-Garland Elementary School from further deterioration of the ambient air and noise quality. Further it protects them from the potential safety hazard of a vehicle gone out of control travelling on the proposed spur.
This is 100% Recycled Priper

Mr. I. C. Herried August 8, 1973 Page two
5
4. Finally, it will be a suitable compromise to so many of my constituents who have opposed this project for so long.
I find these objections to your proposal:
1. You have not made a convincing case for spending $12.1 million for an expressway-type facility that will cover only 1.5 miles. I have always been very conscious of fiscal responsibility and I find expenditures like this too outlandish to take seriously. According to your own superiors, the State Highway System is being pinched today by the lack of money. Proposals like this make me wonder who to believe.
2. Nowhere in this impact statement have I found any discussion or description of the savings in travel time by class of vehicles. In this proposal you are asking the citizens of this state to invest $12.1 million for a one and a half mile road without telling them how much time it is going to save them.
3. Although unfamiliar with your system planning criteria, a prediction of only 18,800 trips per day does not seem to justify a four-lane divided facility.
4. I must sympathize with the views of those constituents of mine who maintain that only under very special circumstances shall a highway facility be constructed that has such high potential for disrupting the learning process of our most valuable resource, our children.
5. Your statements concerning the noise standards do not belie the fact that the airport spur will contribute to an exceeding of the noise standards in many areas near the project.
If there were no other alternatives open to the Highway Division, I would concede your point and withdraw my opposition. However, I feel that my alternative is a viable one and I insist that it be given proper consideration before the submittal and approval of the final environmental impact statement. I am familiar with the requirements of the National and Wisconsin Environmental Impact Acts which require a showing of all the alternatives of environmental impact.
I respectfully request the Division of Highways to:
1. Conduct a feasibility study of my proposal as stated above including in such a study a cost comparison between my proposal and the present proposal.
2. Information regarding the savings in travel time due to the proposed airport spur and the savings in real dollars occurring from the shorter travel time by class of vehicle.

Mr. I. C. Herried August 8, 1973 Page three
3. Include the cost comparison; the breakdown of costs to each level of government: federal, state, county, and local between the two proposals.
1
As I read your impact statement, the main justifications for the project as proposed are to reduce travel time and provide safer access to and from the airport. I believe my proposal can accomplish these purposes as well as at a lower cost to the taxpayer.
Thank you for your interest and attention to this matter.
Sincerely,
JOHN R. PLEWA State Representative
20th District
